messages:
jess: Heads up — EmitLabs (acct_acct_9X) opened a ticket: sudden 429s and p95 spikes starting ~10:02 UTC across /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Customer says traffic jumped but they didn’t change code.

jess: Quick summary from support: baseline ~150rps, spiked to ~1.3k rps for ~6m, then sustained 600rps. They see intermittent 429s and some requests timing out. Attached headers show x-rw-rate-limit remaining hitting 0. Need triage and root-cause attribution.

oliver: @jess can you paste a sample response & request headers and the Grafana panel link? want to see whether it’s per-route or per-customer quota. :rotating_light:

jess: Here — sample curl that the customer ran and the 429 response snippet:
```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_emitlabs' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-base-8k","input":"hello"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 60000
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 165
content-type: application/json
```

jess: Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/8a7J/requests-by-route?from=now-30m&to=now
Query used: sum(increase(api.requests_total{status_code="429"}[5m])) by (route, account_id)

maya: I pulled the quota config for acct_acct_9X — they’re on Dedicated with a per-minute token quota + burst_allowance. Burst_allowance was fully consumed at 10:05 according to the lease metrics. Looks like an inbound traffic burst filled the token bucket; afterwards rate limiter returned 429s until tokens replenished.

maya: Snippet from quota-store:
```
account: acct_acct_9X
mode: dedicated
rate_limit: 1000 rpm (tokens per minute)
burst_allowance: 2500 tokens
current_burst: 0
```

oliver: That matches. Two immediate attribution steps: 1) correlate 429 spikes with x-rw-rate-limit-remaining==0 in logs, 2) break down by route and model to see which route consumed tokens fastest. I queried logs and saw 85% of 429s attributed to route="/v1/embeddings" and model=fast-embed-2.

oliver: Datadog log query I ran:
```
logs("status:429 AND account_id:acct_acct_9X").group_by(["route","model"]).rollup("count", 300)
```

ben: For dashboards/alerts: we should make an alert that fires when a customer has >100 429s in 5m OR x-rw-rate-limit-remaining==0 for >2 minutes. Also add a panel showing top (route, model) pairs by 429s for last 1h.

sam: Customer asked for repro steps so they can confirm. I suggested a safe repro that simulates burst without using prod key repeatedly — they can use their staging account. Example repro (throttle-friendly):
```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do \
  curl -s -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings' -H 'Authorization: Bearer SK_STAGING' -d '{"model":"fast-embed-2","input":"test"}' &
  if (( i % 200 == 0 )); then sleep 1; fi
done
```

sam: They tried a similar loop in prod which saturated their burst_allowance quickly. We recommended staged ramp and watch x-rw-rate-limit headers.

oliver: Operational playbook to attribute quickly:
1) Filter logs by account_id and HTTP 429s.
2) Group by route and model — top pair likely consumer.
3) Cross-check quota-store for account config + burst usage.
4) Check our autoscaler/queue backpressure for any backlog that might cause token usage to appear higher (e.g., retries).

oliver: Example quick query (Grafana/Prometheus):
```
sum(rate(api_response_status_count{account_id="acct_acct_9X",status_code="429"}[5m])) by (route, model)
```

jess: Customer also reported elevated latency before 429s. Could be retries from client or large embedding payloads. I asked them to share a few request sizes.

maya: Also worth noting: some model variants (quantized) have much lower per-token CPU so they're cheaper; customer switched model at 09:59 which caused a temporary concurrency spike to the embeddings route. That explains the sudden burst.

ben: Action items:
- Increase provisional burst_allowance for acct_acct_9X to avoid immediate customer impact (maya)
- Add alert rule for per-account sustained x-rw-rate-limit-remaining==0 (oliver)
- Update runbook with the quick attribution queries (jess + oliver)
- Customer follow-up: recommend model/routing changes and repro guidance (sam)

oncall-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-934 (priority: P2) — assigned to oliver.

grafana-bot: Panel snapshot posted: https://grafana.redwood.local/d-snapshot/abcd1234 (top routes by 429s, last 60m)

jess: Thanks team — I’ll message the customer with repro guidance, temporary quota bump, and timeline for full analysis. Will post logs here when they send the request samples. :thumbsup:

oliver: If they want immediate relief and are on Dedicated, we can temporarily raise the quota and set a short-term policy to route low-priority calls to a cheaper model variant to spread load.

sam: Customer confirmed staging repro and accepts a temporary quota bump. Closing loop after post-analysis.
